lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Alright, let us get going, James has a hard stop at four. The goal today is to lock the structure of the new pricing page so Leah can start on high fidelity designs this week.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Hard stop at four ten, technically. But yeah, let us be quick.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Sofia, do you want to start with the data?

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Sure. So quick context. The pricing page gets about eighteen thousand visits a month. Visit to trial conversion is two point one percent, which is below the benchmark we keep quoting, which is somewhere around three to four percent for B2B analytics.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: And from the session recordings, the thing that jumps out is people scrolling back and forth between Growth and Enterprise. Like, a lot. The average time on page is almost three minutes, which sounds good but I think it means people are confused.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Yeah, I watched maybe forty of those recordings. People hover over the Enterprise column, then click contact sales, then bounce off the form. The form has nine fields, which, honestly, is a crime.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Hey, I need those fields.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Do you need company revenue range though? Really?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Okay, fine, not that one. But I need company size and monthly event volume, otherwise my reps waste the first call on qualification.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Let us park the form for a second, we will come back to it. The first big question is whether we show a price for Enterprise.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: My view is we should show a starting price. Something like starting at two thousand dollars a month. Right now there is a massive gap between Growth at four ninety nine and a black box, and people do not know if Enterprise is three thousand or thirty thousand.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I really do not love that. The moment you put a number up, every deal anchors on it. Our median Enterprise deal last quarter was around forty two thousand a year, so about thirty five hundred a month, and some of those started as conversations about fifteen hundred.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: But that is kind of my point. If the median is thirty five hundred and we say starting at two thousand, we are not underselling anything --

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: -- you are, though. Because procurement will grab the two thousand and say, your own website says two thousand.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: What about the customers who never contact us at all because they assume it is too expensive? We do not see them in the pipeline, so we do not count them.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Sure, but those folks are probably not Enterprise buyers anyway.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Can I throw out a middle ground? What if we do not show a price, but we show what drives the price. Like, priced on annual event volume and seats, with typical plans for teams of fifty plus. It at least tells people how it works.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Hmm. That is better than today, for sure.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I could live with that. I would even be okay saying most customers start with a twelve month agreement.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay, let us do this. We ship Leah's version, the explanation of what drives price, no number. And Sofia, can you set it up as an A B test against a version with a starting at price? Then we let the data settle it instead of us arguing.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Yes. We need about six weeks to get significance at our traffic levels, just so everyone knows.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Fine. But if the starting price version wins on trials and my average deal size drops, we revisit.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Deal. We measure trial starts and qualified pipeline, not just clicks. Okay, second topic. The usage based events tier.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Right. So today Growth includes five million events a month, and above that we bill forty dollars per extra million, in arrears. Customers find out when the invoice lands. It is super manual and everyone hates it.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: It is a nightmare. My team spent, I kid you not, about sixty hours last month on overage conversations.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: So the proposal is a cheaper, predictable overage on Growth. Something like twenty five dollars per additional million events, billed monthly, with alerts at eighty and a hundred percent.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: What is the margin on that? Arjun mentioned our cost per million events is going up because of the ClickHouse cluster.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Arjun estimated our fully loaded cost at about three dollars per million today. So twenty five gives us healthy margin. I checked Mixpanel and Amplitude, and twenty five is roughly in the middle.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Design wise, I would love a little calculator on the page. You drag a slider for your monthly events and it shows you the estimated bill. People love those.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: As long as the slider tops out at like fifty million and then says talk to us. Anyone above that is an Enterprise conversation.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Yep, that works. Above fifty million it switches to a contact sales card.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Okay, I think that is a decision. Growth gets overage at twenty five per million, calculator on the page capped at fifty million. Any objections?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: None. Please ship it yesterday.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Ha. Okay, third thing, annual discount. Today it is twenty percent. Sofia, you wanted to change it?

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Yeah. So twenty percent is generous. Most of our peers are at fifteen or seventeen. And our annual uptake is already sixty one percent on Growth, so I do not think we need to bribe people that hard.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I disagree, strongly. The twenty percent is one of the main reasons we get annual commitments, and annual customers churn at less than half the rate of monthly. Cash up front is also, you know, nice for runway.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Do we have the numbers on that churn claim?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Siobhan pulled them last month. Monthly Growth logos churn about three point four percent a month. Annual is closer to one point two, annualized to monthly.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: But that is correlation. The people who pick annual were probably more committed anyway.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Sure, but you cannot prove that either.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: This feels like another candidate for a test, honestly.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I do not want to run two pricing tests at the same time, it muddies the results. Here is my call. We keep twenty percent for now. We revisit in Q1 once the Enterprise test is done. Sofia, I know that is not what you wanted.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: It is fine. I would just like it noted that I think we are leaving roughly forty thousand a year on the table.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Noted. Literally, it is being recorded.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Ha. Okay, back to the form?

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Yes please. I want to cut it from nine fields to four. Name, work email, company size, and monthly event volume as a dropdown. Everything else we can enrich from the email domain.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I can accept that if we keep a free text field for what are you trying to solve. My reps actually read those.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Optional free text field. Five fields total, one optional. Final offer.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Sold.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Great. One more small thing, the comparison table. It currently has forty two rows. Nobody reads forty two rows.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: I want to collapse it to eight key rows by default with a show all features toggle. And I want to put AI Insights in there as coming soon for Growth and Enterprise.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Hmm, careful with that. We have not decided if AI Insights is going to be included in Growth or an add on. If we say it is included and then charge for it, people will be annoyed.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Good call. Leave AI Insights off the page until the Q4 roadmap meeting settles packaging. Just put a teaser banner, no tier assignment.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Okay, teaser banner, no tiers. Got it.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Let me recap owners and dates. Leah, high fidelity designs for the new page including the calculator, by next Wednesday.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Yep, I can do that. I will share a Figma link in the pricing channel Monday for early feedback.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Sofia, write the experiment brief for the Enterprise price A B test, with the success metrics, by Friday. And work with Aman on the billing side of overage.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: Brief by Friday, yes. I will book time with Aman tomorrow, I think the Stripe metered billing work is about two sprints.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: James, update the sales playbook and the lead routing for the new five field form, and give the reps a heads up about overage pricing before we launch.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Will do. I will have the playbook updated by the twentieth and I will do a fifteen minute walkthrough at the Monday sales sync.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: And I will write the pricing change announcement for existing Growth customers, since overage affects them. Target launch for the whole thing is November third.

lines.speaker: sofia
lines.text: November third is tight with two sprints of billing work, just flagging.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Noted. Let us check in on it next Thursday and move the date if billing slips. Okay, James, you have made your hard stop with four minutes to spare.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: A miracle. Thanks all.

lines.speaker: leah
lines.text: Bye everyone.
